gap: No result ChatGPT got works out each charger's PPS output at 20 V (the maximum PPS amps × 20 V, which the S26 Ultra needs to reach 60 W) for anything except Samsung's own adapters. None of those results shows that the Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 meets the requirement with one device plugged in (20 V × 5 A = 100 W) but falls to 45 W per port once a second device is plugged in.
standout_why: I compared against ChargerLAB's EP-T6010 teardown (cited), SamMobile's 65W Trio article (cited), SamMobile's 'what you need for 60W', Android Authority's S26 Ultra test and ChargerLAB's S26 Ultra compatibility test. ChargerLAB has the EP-T6010's PPS sets and SamMobile has the Trio's 20 V/2.25 A limit, so the Samsung side is already covered. The two SamMobile pages and Android Authority give the requirement only in general terms and name no third-party charger. The ChargerLAB compatibility test's charger list would not load in the fetch tool, so I could not check it. GSMArena does not name its 67 W charger. None of the rival pages works out the 20 V figure for a third-party charger, and none mentions how sharing ports cuts it.
decides: This confirms Samsung's EP-T6010 as the only charger with a measured S26 Ultra result: 20 V × 3 A = 60 W on PPS, with 51.54 W measured into the phone by ChargerLAB and a 60 W peak and 42 minutes to full by Android Authority. Among chargers we link, the Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 meets the 20 V/3 A requirement on paper with room to spare (20 V × 5 A = 100 W, per techtest.org), but only when the phone is the only device plugged in. With two devices it gives 45 W per port, which is below the 60 W tier. Nobody has tested the AH22 on an S26 Ultra, so the AH22 is a 'meets the requirement on its listed PPS range' row, not a measured pick. Samsung's 65W Trio fails: 20 V × 2.25 A = 45 W. I could not confirm the UGREEN Nexode 65W travel charger this run.
candidates: Samsung 65W Trio Power Adapter (named as the one that does not have it)

findings.label: What the S26 Ultra needs for 60 W
findings.value: USB PD 3.1 charger with PPS and 20 V/3 A from a single port (20 V × 3 A = 60 W)
findings.source_title: Samsung's 60W Galaxy S26 Ultra finally charges fast, but only because it lags on battery size - Android Authority
findings.note: Robert Triggs, 2026-04-06. He adds that PPS is common but 20 V PPS support is 'not so common', and that the bundled 3 A cable is enough (a 5 A cable does not charge faster).

findings.label: Charging curve on the S26 Ultra
findings.value: 60 W peak for about 2 min; about 48 W for about 16 min; 37% at 10 min, 85% at 30 min, full in 42 min
findings.source_title: Samsung's 60W Galaxy S26 Ultra finally charges fast, but only because it lags on battery size - Android Authority
findings.note: The article does not name its charger, but it recommends Samsung's official 60W adapter. Derived: 48 W ÷ 60 W = 80% of the peak during the sustained phase. The 60 W peak lasts 2 of the 42 minutes, about 5%.

findings.label: PPS output at 20 V
findings.value: 60 W (printed PPS 5–20 V at 3 A; measured PPS sets 5–11 V at 5 A, 5–16 V at 4 A, 5–21 V at 3 A)
findings.source_title: Teardown of Samsung 60W Low Standby GaN Charger (EP-T6010) - ChargerLAB
findings.note: Arithmetic: 20 V × 3 A = 60 W. Only the 5–21 V set reaches 20 V. The 5–11 V × 5 A set (55 W) and the 5–16 V × 4 A set (64 W) carry big wattages but cannot give the 20 V mode. Measured with a POWER-Z KM003C.

findings.label: Measured draw into a Galaxy S26 Ultra
findings.source_title: Teardown of Samsung 60W Low Standby GaN Charger (EP-T6010) - ChargerLAB
findings.note: Derived: 51.54 ÷ 60 = 86% of the rated tier. Standby 1.23 mW at 110 V. Size 48.08 × 46.13 × 28.11 mm, weight 103 g.

findings.label: Price, samsung.com US (EP-T6010NBEGUS)
findings.source_title: 60W PD Power Adapter, Black | Samsung US
findings.note: No sale price shown. Delivery and pickup show 'Not Available' until a ZIP code is entered. Derived: $54.99 ÷ 60 W = $0.92 per watt of the 20 V PPS tier. ChatGPT showed Best Buy at $30.77; I did not read Best Buy.

findings.label: PPS output at 20 V (the well-known one that fails)
findings.value: 45 W (20 V × 2.25 A), 15 W short of 60 W
findings.source_title: Samsung's 65W Trio adapter can't charge your Galaxy S26 Ultra at 60W - SamMobile
findings.note: Adnan Farooqui. Arithmetic: 20 V × 2.25 A = 45 W; 60 − 45 = 15 W short, even though the box says 65 W.

findings.label: PPS output at 20 V, one device plugged in
findings.value: 100 W (PPS 5–20 V at up to 5 A on each of USB-C 1, 2 and 3)
findings.source_title: Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 im Test: 100W USB-C-Ladegerät mit Display und AVS - techtest.org
findings.note: Michael Barton, 2026-11-23. Arithmetic: 20 V × 5 A = 100 W ≥ 60 W, so the 20 V/3 A requirement is met on paper. Also lists AVS 9–20 V at 5 A. The reviewer claims Samsung fast charging works but did not test or measure a Samsung phone.

findings.label: Per-port watts with a second device plugged in
findings.value: 45 W + 45 W (two ports); 45 W + 45 W + 10 W (three ports)
findings.source_title: Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 im Test: 100W USB-C-Ladegerät mit Display und AVS - techtest.org
findings.note: Arithmetic: 45 W < 60 W. Once a second device is plugged in, the S26 Ultra cannot reach its 60 W tier from any port. This is the same 45 W the Trio is limited to.

findings.label: Fixed PD output and stated protocols
findings.value: Fixed 5/9/12/15 V at 3 A and 20 V at 3.25 A (65 W); 'supports USB Power Delivery 3.2, including AVS and PPS' with no PPS range given
findings.source_title: Compact, powerful and efficient: Ugreen Nexode Air 65W USB-C GaN charger review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Daniel Schmidt, updated 2026-10-05. A fixed 20 V × 3.25 A does not prove PPS at 20 V, so I cannot work out its 20 V PPS output from this page. Notebookcheck's Elvis Shida (2026-10-07) says the AVS version is a quiet revision ($39.99, Amazon ASIN B0HG147M33) and gives no PPS ranges.
